frameworks.name: IFRS / IAS
frameworks.appliesTo: Listed groups in the UK and many other countries; the base the others are built from.

frameworks.name: FRS 102
frameworks.appliesTo: Most UK private companies; small companies use its Section 1A with fewer disclosures.

frameworks.name: FRS 105
frameworks.appliesTo: Micro-entities that choose the micro-entity regime.

frameworks.name: AASB (Australian standards)
frameworks.appliesTo: Australian entities that must report; for-profit standards mirror IFRS word for word, with extra paragraphs for not-for-profits.

ifrs.summary: One model: almost every lease goes on the balance sheet as a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. Optional exemptions for short-term leases (12 months or less) and low-value assets.

frs102.summary: From periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026 the lessee model follows IFRS 16: right-of-use asset and lease liability, with short-term and low-value exemptions. Before that, operating leases were expensed straight-line and only finance leases were capitalised.

frs105.summary: Keeps the old split: finance leases on the balance sheet, operating lease payments expensed. Check the current FRS 105 text before relying on this, as the Periodic Review 2024 also amended FRS 105.

aasb.summary: Same as IFRS 16, word for word.

topics.takeaway: A UK client moving onto the 2026 FRS 102 will see new assets, new liabilities, higher EBITDA and lease payments split between interest and principal.

ifrs.summary: Five steps: identify the contract, identify the performance obligations, set the price, allocate it, recognise revenue as each obligation is satisfied (at a point in time or over time).

frs102.summary: From 2026, a five-step model based on IFRS 15, with simplifications. Before that, revenue was recognised on transfer of the risks and rewards of ownership, or by stage of completion for services.

frs105.summary: A simplified revenue section. The Periodic Review 2024 aligned it with the new FRS 102 approach in a simpler form; check the current FRS 105 text for detail.

aasb.summary: For-profit entities use AASB 15 (same as IFRS 15). Not-for-profits also apply AASB 1058 to income such as grants and donations where there is no enforceable obligation to transfer goods or services.

topics.takeaway: In practice the timing changes most for bundled contracts: a sale of hardware plus a year's support becomes two obligations.

ifrs.summary: Never amortised. Tested for impairment every year, and whenever there is an indicator.

frs102.summary: Amortised over its useful life. If the life cannot be reliably estimated, it must not exceed 10 years. Impairment tested when there is an indicator.

frs105.summary: Amortised, on the same 10-year default when the life cannot be estimated.

aasb.summary: Same as IFRS: no amortisation, annual impairment test.

topics.takeaway: A UK subsidiary of an Australian group amortises goodwill locally, and the group reverses that amortisation on consolidation.

ifrs.summary: Research is always expensed. Development must be capitalised once all six criteria are met (feasibility, intention, ability, future benefit, resources, reliable measurement).

frs102.summary: Research is expensed. Development that meets the criteria may be capitalised or expensed: an accounting policy choice, applied consistently.

frs105.summary: Research and development are expensed; internally generated intangible assets are not recognised.

aasb.summary: Same as IAS 38: capitalise when the criteria are met.

topics.takeaway: UK software companies often choose to expense development under FRS 102 to keep the books simple, then claim R&D tax relief separately.

ifrs.summary: Lower of cost and net realisable value. Cost by FIFO or weighted average (specific identification for unique items). LIFO is not allowed.

frs102.summary: Lower of cost and estimated selling price less costs to complete and sell. FIFO or weighted average; LIFO is not allowed.

frs105.summary: Same measurement idea, simpler wording and disclosures. LIFO is not allowed.

aasb.summary: Same as IAS 2. Not-for-profits hold inventory for distribution at cost adjusted for loss of service potential.

topics.takeaway: Everywhere this site covers, LIFO is prohibited. Use the Inventory tool to see FIFO and weighted average side by side.

ifrs.summary: Cost model or revaluation model, by class of asset. Significant components depreciated separately. Residual value and useful life reviewed at least every year end.

frs102.summary: Cost model or revaluation model. Components depreciated separately when they have very different lives. Residual value and life reviewed when there is an indication of change.

frs105.summary: Cost model only. Revaluation and fair value accounting are not allowed for micro-entities.

aasb.summary: Same as IAS 16, with not-for-profit paragraphs (e.g. assets received for nil consideration).

topics.takeaway: A capitalisation threshold (e.g. 'items under $1,000 are expensed') is an internal materiality policy, not a rule of the standard. The tax write-off limit is a separate, tax-only rule.

ifrs.summary: Interest that relates directly to building a qualifying asset must be capitalised into its cost.

frs102.summary: Policy choice: capitalise borrowing costs on qualifying assets, or expense them all.

topics.takeaway: Mostly relevant to property developers and businesses building their own premises.

ifrs.summary: Statement of financial position, profit or loss and OCI, changes in equity, cash flows, and notes. IFRS 18 replaces IAS 1 for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027, with new defined subtotals in profit or loss.

frs102.summary: The same statements, but small companies using Section 1A need not present a cash flow statement or statement of changes in equity and give far fewer notes.

frs105.summary: A balance sheet and a profit and loss account with very few notes. No cash flow statement.

aasb.summary: AASB 101 mirrors IAS 1, and AASB 18 mirrors IFRS 18. Entities that are not publicly accountable may use Simplified Disclosures (AASB 1060) instead of full disclosure.

topics.takeaway: The bookkeeping is the same everywhere; what changes is how much the year-end pack has to disclose.
